notes.R1: A test of R1 asserts exactly R-acronym's two example outputs ('NASA Rocket Launch', 'Read The HTTP Spec') on input that also contains lowercase letters and leaves no-lowercase input to R5, so it checks R-acronym and does not contradict R-all-caps-input.
notes.R2: Extra titleize-preservation invariant limited to inputs in which every uppercase letter is immediately followed by a lowercase letter, a domain with no all-caps word and no fully uppercase input, so its tests check none of the reference requirements and conflict with none.
notes.R5: A test of R5 asserts titleize('HELLO WORLD') == 'Hello World' and base-identical output for inputs with no lowercase letters, which is R-all-caps-input; its sentence limiting acronym-keeping to inputs with lowercase letters restates R-acronym's scope, but its tests use only no-lowercase inputs and so do not exercise R-acronym.
notes.R6: A test of R6 asserts humanize('employee_salary') == 'Employee salary' and runs a differential test of humanize against the base implementation, which is R-humanize-unchanged.
notes.R7: A test of R7 checks that underscore('NASARocket') and other inputs give the base implementation's output, which is R-underscore-unchanged; its parenthetical base value 'nasa_rocket' matches what upstream inflection's underscore returns and the requirement is tied to the base output either way, so there is no contradiction.
